sentences.text: Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of Motor  Vehicles Act, 1988, against the judgment and decree dated 22.06.201  in MACT. OP.No.1746 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claim  Tribunal, Salem, Special Sub Court-I, Salem.
For Appellant : Mr.Arun  for M/s. Karan and Uday  JUDGMENT
This appellant/claimant has come forward with this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation by challenging the decree and judgment dated 22.06.2016 made in MACT.
OP.No.1746 of 2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Salem, Special Sub Court-I, Salem.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.Brief fact which are necessary for disposal of this appeal is as follows:-
On 05.06.2011 at about 3.10 P.M., when the appellant was driving his motor cycle bearing Registration No.TN 54 Y 5343 from Vadukarthampatty to Poosaripatti, at that time, a Government Bus No.88, TSTC bearing Registration No.TN 27 N 1644 came in the opposite direction near Rajapattinam from Salem to Belur driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the appellant, due to that, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.

Thereby, the appellant/claimant has filed a Rajesh vs M/S.Tamil Nadu State Transport ... on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121036617/
1 claim Petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.14,00,000/-
against the Transport Corporation.
3.

entities.text: Rajesh vs M/S.Tamil Nadu State Transport
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before the Tribunal, during trial, in order to prove the case, on the side of the appellant, two witnesses were examined viz., PW1 and PW2 and marked 12 documents viz., Exs.P1 to P12, On the side of the respondent/Transport Corporation
, one witness was examined and one document was marked.

The Tribunal, considering the pleadings, oral and documentary evidence, allowed the petition in part and awarded a sum of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rs.4,59,500/-
compensation to the claimant.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant has filed this appeal before this Court for enhancement of the compensation.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the appellant has sustained grievous injuries all over the body and his right side thigh bone was fractured and he was undergone surgery.

Without considering the same, the Tribunal has erred in awarding a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-
towards disability.
The appellant could not continue his avocation after the accident.

The Tribunal did not consider the gravity of injuries as well as impact and consequences of the injuries and awarded meager amount under the heads of loss of income and loss of amenities, attender charges and transportation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent/Transport Corporation submitted that the the the appellant has sustained only simple injuries and therefore, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation towards disability is reasonable and other heads awarded by the Tribunal are also just a n d p r o p e r , w h i c h c a n n o t b e i n t e r f e r e d w i t h . H e n c e , t h i s C o u r t m a y https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
dismiss the appeal.
6. This Court gave its careful consideration to the submissions advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and perused the materials available on record.
7. The factum of the accident is not disputed by the parties and so also the liability.
Therefore, this Court is not entering into the said aspect.
The only grievance of the claimant is with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded.
8. On perusal of the award, it is seen that the appellant, before the Tribunal, the appellant has not produced the disability certificate.
The Tribunal, after considering the medical records, assessed 50% disability to the appellant and awarded Rs.5000/- per percentage, which is reasonable and the same does not warrant any interference.
According to the appellant, he was aged about 20 years at the time of the accident and he has worked as a driller and agriculturist.
To prove the income, the appellant has not produced any document before the Tribunal.
Even then the Tribunal has https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis awarded Rs.30,000/- in respect of income during treatment period, which is perfectly in order.
Further, the compensation awarded under other heads are just and reasonable, which needs no interference.

The Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, after deducting the amount if any already deposited within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
